verses.translation: Dhritarashtra said, "What did my people and the sons of Pandu do when they had assembled together, eager for battle, on the holy plain of Kurukshetra, O Sanjaya?"
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield
verses.theme: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened on the battlefield of Kurukshetra
verses.meaning: The blind king asks his minister to describe the assembled armies — the opening moment of doubt and moral conflict before a great struggle.

verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having seen the army of the Pandavas drawn up in battle array, King Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona, and spoke these words.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Behold, O Teacher! This mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna, Yuyudhana (Satyaki), Virata, and Drupada—all mighty warriors.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the valiant king of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Saibya—the best of men.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: The strong Yudhamanyu and the brave Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra and Arjuna), and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great charioteers (great heroes)."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Know also, O best among the twice-born! the names of those who are the most distinguished amongst ourselves, the leaders of my army; these I name to you for your information.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: "Thou thyself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, the victorious in war, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and Bhurisrava, the son of Somadatta—all these are ready for battle."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: And also many other heroes, ready to give up their lives for my sake, armed with various weapons and missiles, all well-skilled in battle.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Our army, marshalled by Bhishma, is insufficient, whereas theirs, marshalled by Bhima, is sufficient.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Therefore, do all of you, stationed in your respective positions in the several divisions of the army, protect Bhishma alone.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: His glorious grandsire, the oldest of the Kauravas, roared like a lion to cheer Duryodhana and blew his conch.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Then, suddenly, conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums, and cow horns blared forth from the Kaurava side, and the sound was tremendous.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Then, Madhava (Krishna) and the son of Pandu (Arjuna), seated in the magnificent chariot yoked with white horses, blew divine conches.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Hrishikesha blew the Panchajanya, Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima, the wolf-bellied doer of terrible deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: The king of Kasi, an excellent archer, Sikhandi, the mighty car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the unconquered.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of the Earth, and the son of Subhadra, the mighty-armed, blew their conches each separately.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: The tumultuous sound rent the hearts of Dhritarashtra's party, reverberating through both heaven and earth.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Then, seeing the people of Dhritarashtra's party standing arrayed and the discharge of weapons about to begin, Arjuna, the son of Pandu whose ensign was a monkey, took up his bow and said the following to Krishna, O Lord of the Earth.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, place my chariot in the middle between the two armies, so that I may behold those who stand here, desirous to fight, and know with whom I must fight when the battle is about to commence."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, place my chariot in the middle between the two armies, so that I may behold those who stand here, desirous to fight, and know with whom I must fight when the battle is about to commence."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: For I desire to observe those who are assembled here to fight, wishing to please in battle the evil-minded Duryodhana—the son of Dhritarashtra.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Sanjaya said, Thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna stationed the best of chariots, O Dhritarashtra, in the midst of the two armies.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: In front of Bhishma and Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, he said: "O Arjuna, son of Pritha, behold these Kurus gathered together."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Then, Arjuna (son of Pritha) saw there (in the armies) stationed fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: He saw fathers-in-law and friends in both the armies. The son of Kunti, Arjuna, seeing all those kinsmen thus standing arrayed, spoke sorrowfully, deeply filled with pity.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, seeing my kinsmen arrayed here, eager to fight,
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield
verses.theme: Arjuna sees his loved ones on the opposing side and breaks down
verses.meaning: Arjuna sees his teachers, uncles and cousins arrayed against him and is overcome with compassion and sorrow — his bow slips, his heart fails. This is the human moment before every hard decision.

verses.translation: My limbs fail, my mouth is parched, my body quivers, and my hair stands on end.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: The Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over; I am unable to stand, and my mind is reeling, as it were.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: And I see ill omens, O Kesava. I do not see any good in slaying my kinsmen in battle.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation:
I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.
What use is dominion to us, O Krishna, or pleasures or even life?
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures stand here in battle, having renounced life and wealth.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives—
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: These I do not wish to kill, O Krishna, even though they kill me, for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; leave alone killing them for the sake of the earth."
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure could be ours, O Janardana? Only sin would accrue to us from killing these felons.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield
verses.theme: Arjuna questions the point of killing his own people for a kingdom
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks — what pleasure can come from killing our own kinsmen? Is a kingdom worth this? The question anyone faces when doing what is right will hurt people they love.

verses.translation: Therefore, we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our relatives; for how can we be happy by killing our own kin, O Madhava (Krishna)?
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Though they, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see no evil in the destruction of families and no sin in hostility to friends,
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Why should we not, who clearly see the evil in the destruction of families, learn to turn away from this sin, O Janardana (Krishna)?
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: In the destruction of a family, the immemorial religious rites of that family perish; on the destruction of spirituality, impiety indeed, overwhelms the whole family.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: O Krishna, by the prevalence of impiety, the women of the family become corrupt; and, when women are corrupted, O Varshenya (descendant of Vrishni), intermingling of castes arises.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Confusion of castes leads to hell for the slayers of the family, for their forebears fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and libations of water.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: By these evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, which cause confusion of castes, the eternal religious rites of the caste and the family are destroyed.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: We have heard, O Janardana, that those men in whose families the religious practices have been destroyed are inevitably destined to dwell in hell for an unknown period.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Alas! We are involved in a great sin, for we are prepared to kill our kinsmen, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, should slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield

verses.translation: Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken in the midst of the battlefield, Arjuna cast away his bow and arrow and, his mind overwhelmed with sorrow, sat down on the seat of the chariot.
verses.chTheme: Arjuna's grief and moral confusion on the battlefield
verses.theme: Arjuna collapses in grief, unable to act
verses.meaning: Arjuna drops his bow and sits down in the chariot, overwhelmed by grief — unable to act. The image of complete paralysis before a necessary but painful duty.

verses.translation: Sanjaya said: To him, who was thus overcome with pity, despondent, with eyes full of tears and agitated, Madhusudana (the destroyer of Madhu) or Krishna spoke these words.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "From whence has this perilous strait come upon you, this dejection which is unworthy of you, disgraceful, and which will close the gates of heaven upon you, O Arjuna?"
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Do not yield to impotence, O Arjuna, son of Pritha. It does not befit you. Cast off this mean weakness of the heart! Stand up, O conqueror of foes!
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Do not yield to weakness — arise
verses.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna directly: this weakness does not suit you. Arise. Do not yield to impotence and faint-heartedness. Use when someone is collapsing under pressure and needs a direct call to courage.

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Madhusudana, how can I fight in battle with arrows against Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of being worshipped, O destroyer of enemies?"
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Better it is, indeed, in this world to accept alms than to slay the most noble teachers. But if I were to kill them, even in this world, all my enjoyments of wealth and fulfilled desires would be stained with their blood.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: I can hardly tell which would be better, that we should conquer them or that they should conquer us. Even the sons of Dhritarashtra, whom we do not wish to slay, stand facing us.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: My heart is overpowered by the taint of pity; my mind is confused as to my duty. I ask Thee: Tell me decisively what is good for me. I am Thy disciple; instruct me, who has taken refuge in Thee.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: I am confused about my duty — guide me
verses.meaning: Arjuna admits he is overwhelmed and confused about what is right. He asks Krishna to be his teacher. The moment of surrendering ego and asking for help — a sign of wisdom, not weakness.

verses.translation: I do not see that this sorrow that burns up my senses would be removed, even if I were to attain prosperous and unrivaled dominion on earth or lordship over the gods.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, the Lord of the senses, Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and destroyer of foes, said, "I will not fight," and became silent.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: To him who was despondent in the midst of the two armies, Krishna, smiling, O Bharata, spoke these words.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for; yet, you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead."
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The wise do not grieve for the living or the dead
verses.meaning: Krishna gently points out that the truly wise grieve neither for the living nor the dead — because the soul is eternal. A starting point for conversations about grief and loss.

verses.translation: Nor, at any time, was I not, nor thou, nor these rulers of men; nor, verily, shall we ever cease to be hereafter.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body; the steadfast one does not grieve over this.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The contact of the senses with the objects, O son of Kunti, which causes heat and cold, pleasure and pain, has a beginning and an end; they are impermanent; endure them bravely, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Pleasure and pain are impermanent — endure them
verses.meaning: Sensations of heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go — they are not permanent. They arise from sense contact. Endure them with patience. For anyone suffering and needing perspective that this moment will pass.

verses.translation: That firm man, whom surely these afflictions do not, O chief among men, to whom pleasure and pain are the same, is fit for attaining immortality.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The unreal has no being; there is no non-being of the real; the truth about both has been seen by the knowers of the truth (or the seers of the essence).
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Know that to be indestructible, by which all this is pervaded. No one can cause the destruction of that, the Imperishable.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The soul is indestructible — nothing can destroy it
verses.meaning: That which pervades the entire body is indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable soul. For anyone wrestling with questions of identity, mortality, or what is real.

verses.translation: These bodies of the embodied Self, which are eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable, are said to have an end. Therefore, fight, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: He who takes the Self to be the slayer and he who thinks it is slain, neither of them knows. It does not slay, nor is it slain.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Neither killer nor killed — the soul is beyond action
verses.meaning: He who thinks this soul kills and he who thinks it is killed — both are ignorant. The soul neither kills nor is killed. For someone devastated by a death or by having to cause harm.

verses.translation: It is not born, nor does it ever die; after having been, it again does not cease to be; unborn, eternal, changeless, and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The soul is never born and never dies
verses.meaning: The soul is never born nor does it ever die. It has not come into being and will not come into being. It is unborn, eternal, ever-existing. For existential fear of death or loss of self.

verses.translation: Whoever knows it to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and inexhaustible, how can that person slay, O Arjuna, or cause to be slain?
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so too the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The soul changes bodies like changing clothes
verses.meaning: As a person puts on new garments and gives up old ones, the soul similarly accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones. For major life transitions or letting go of a former self.

verses.translation: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, wind cannot dry it.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: No weapon, fire, water or wind can harm the soul
verses.meaning: No weapon can pierce the soul. No fire can burn it. No water can wet it. No wind can dry it. The deepest comfort for grief — the soul of who we love is beyond all harm.

verses.translation: This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, nor dried up; it is eternal, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, and ancient.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: This Self is said to be unmanifested, unthinkable, and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing this to be so, you should not grieve.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: But even if thou thinkest of It as constantly being born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed one, thou shouldst not grieve.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: For the born, death is certain, and for the dead, birth is certain; therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Death is certain for the born — rebirth is certain for the dead
verses.meaning: For one who has taken their birth, death is certain. And for the dead, birth is certain. Do not grieve over the inevitable. For accepting loss with grace.

verses.translation: Beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their middle state, O Arjuna, and unmanifest again in their end. What is there to grieve about?
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: One sees this (the Self) as a wonder; another speaks of it as a wonder; another hears of it as a wonder; yet, having heard, none understands it at all.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: This indweller in the body of everyone is ever indestructible, O Arjuna; therefore, you should not grieve for any creature.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Further, having regard to your duty, you should not waver, for there is nothing higher for a Kshatriya than a righteous war.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna! who are called to fight in such a battle that comes of its own accord as an open door to heaven.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: But if you will not fight this righteous war, then having abandoned your own duty and reputation, you will incur sin.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: People will also recount your everlasting dishonor; and for one who has been honored, dishonor is worse than death.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The great chariot-warriors will think that you have withdrawn from the battle out of fear, and you will be held in low esteem by those who have held you in high regard.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Your enemies, scoffing at your power, will speak many abusive words—what could be more painful than this?
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Slain, you will obtain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth; therefore, stand up, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat equal, engage in battle for the sake of battle; thus, you shall not incur sin.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss equally — then fight
verses.meaning: Treating alike happiness and distress, loss and gain, victory and defeat — in this way engage in battle and you will not incur sin. For someone paralysed by fear of outcomes.

verses.translation: This, which has been taught to you, is wisdom concerning Sankhya. Now listen to wisdom concerning Yoga, endowed with which, O Arjuna, you shall cast off the bonds of action.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: In this, there is no loss of effort, nor is there any harm produced, nor any transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects one from great fear.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: No effort on the spiritual path is lost
verses.meaning: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution. Even a little of this knowledge saves one from the greatest danger. For someone who feels their efforts are too small or too late.

verses.translation: Here, O joy of the Kurus, there is only one single-pointed determination; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the indecisive.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The resolute mind has one focus — the irresolute mind branches endlessly
verses.meaning: Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose — their aim is one. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless. For someone paralysed by too many choices.

verses.translation: The unwise, taking pleasure in the eulogizing words of the Vedas, utter flowery speech, saying, "There is nothing else," O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Full of desires, with heaven as their goal, (they speak words that are directed to ends) leading to new births as the result of their works, and prescribe various methods abounding in specific actions, for the attainment of pleasure and power.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: For those who are attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are drawn away by such teachings, their determinate reason is not formed which is steadily bent on meditation and Samadhi (superconscious state).
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes. O Arjuna, free yourself from the pairs of opposites and ever remain in the quality of Sattva, freed from acquisition and preservation, and be established in the Self.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: To the Brahmana who has known the Self, all the Vedas are of as much use as a reservoir of water would be in a place where there is a flood.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Your right is only to work, but not to its results; do not let the results of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Right to action but not to its fruits
verses.meaning: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Do not consider yourself the cause of results, nor be attached to inaction. The foundational verse for work stress and outcome anxiety.

verses.translation: Perform action, O Arjuna, being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and balanced in success and failure; evenness of mind is called Yoga.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Perform action with an even mind — this is yoga
verses.meaning: Perform your duty equipoised, abandoning all attachment to success or failure — such equanimity is called yoga. For someone who needs to detach from outcomes while still doing their best work.

verses.translation: Far lower than the Yoga of wisdom is action, O Arjuna. Seek thou refuge in wisdom; wretched are those whose motive is the fruit.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Endowed with wisdom and evenness of mind, one casts off in this life both good and evil deeds; therefore, devote yourself to Yoga; Yoga is skill in action.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The wise, possessing knowledge, having abandoned the fruits of their actions, and being freed from the bonds of birth, go to the place which is beyond all evil.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: When your intellect passes beyond the mire of delusion, then you will attain indifference to what has been heard and what has yet to be heard.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: When your intellect, which is perplexed by the Vedic texts you have read, stands immovable and steady in the Self, then you will attain Self-realization.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, what is the description of one who has steady wisdom and is merged in the superconscious state? How does one of steady wisdom speak, how do they sit, and how do they walk?"
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "When a man completely casts off, O Arjuna, all the desires of the mind and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then he is said to be one of steady wisdom."
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The wise person who has given up all desires of the mind is steady
verses.meaning: When a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is satisfied in the self by the self alone — they are called a person of steady wisdom. For someone exhausted by wanting.

verses.translation: He whose mind is not shaken by adversity, who does not long for pleasures, and is free from attachment, fear, and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: He who is everywhere without attachment, upon encountering anything good or bad, neither rejoices nor hastens; his wisdom is firm.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: When, like the tortoise which withdraws all its limbs on all sides, he withdraws his senses from the sense-objects, then his wisdom becomes steady.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: Withdraw senses from objects like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs
verses.meaning: When a person withdraws the senses from sense objects — like a tortoise pulling its limbs within its shell — their wisdom becomes steady. For anyone overwhelmed by distraction or digital noise.

verses.translation: The objects of the senses turn away from the abstinent man, leaving the longing behind; but his longing also turns away upon seeing the Supreme.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, can violently carry away the mind of a wise person, even though they are striving to control them.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Having restrained them all, he should sit steadfast, intent on Me; his wisdom is steady whose senses are under control.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: One who restrains the senses and fixes the mind gains steady wisdom
verses.meaning: One who restrains all the senses and fixes the mind on me — their wisdom is steady. For building mental discipline and daily spiritual practice.

verses.translation: When one thinks of objects, attachment to them arises; from attachment, desire is born; from desire, anger arises.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: From dwelling on sense objects comes attachment then desire then anger
verses.meaning: While contemplating sense objects, attachment develops. From attachment comes desire. From desire comes anger. From anger — delusion. For someone who wants to understand where their anger actually comes from.

verses.translation: Anger leads to delusion, which causes loss of memory; this, in turn, leads to the destruction of discrimination, resulting in destruction.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: From anger comes delusion and total ruin of reason
verses.meaning: From anger comes delusion. From delusion comes confused memory. From confused memory comes the destruction of intelligence. And from destruction of intelligence one falls again into the material pool. For someone whose anger is destroying their life.

verses.translation: But the self-controlled man, moving among objects with the senses restrained and free from attraction and repulsion, attains peace.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: In that peace, all pains are destroyed; for the intellect of the tranquil-minded soon becomes steady.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: There is no knowledge of the Self for the unsteady, and no meditation is possible for the unsteady, and no peace for the unmeditative, and how can there be happiness for one who has no peace?
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: For the mind, which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, carries away his discrimination, as the wind carries away a boat on the waters.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed Arjuna, his knowledge is steady whose senses are completely restrained from sense objects.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man is awake; when all beings are awake, that is night for the sage who sees.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: He attains peace into whom all desires enter, just as waters enter the ocean which, filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the man who is full of desires.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results
verses.theme: The peaceful ocean receives rivers without being disturbed — the wise person receives desires the same way
verses.meaning: As the ocean remains undisturbed though rivers constantly flow into it — one who is not disturbed by the flow of desires achieves peace. Not one who strives to fulfill them. For someone overwhelmed by their own wants and needs.

verses.translation: That person attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves about without longing, without the sense of ownership, and without egoism.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: O son of Pritha, this is the eternal state, the Brahmic seat. Attaining this, one is not deluded. Being established in it, one attains oneness with Brahman even at the end of life.
verses.chTheme: Sankhya philosophy — eternal soul, duty, detachment from results

verses.translation: Arjuna said: If Thou thinkest that knowledge is superior to action, O Krishna, why then, O Kesava, doest Thou ask me to engage in this terrible action?
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: With this seemingly perplexing speech, you seem to be confusing my understanding; therefore, tell me one certain way by which I may attain bliss.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "In this world, there is a twofold path, as I said before, O sinless one: the path of knowledge of the Sankhyas and the path of action of the Yogins."
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Man does not reach actionlessness by not performing actions; nor does he attain perfection by mere renunciation.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Verily, no one can remain for even a moment without performing action; for everyone is made to act helplessly, indeed, by the qualities born of Nature.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking of the sense-objects in his mind, he of deluded understanding is called a hypocrite.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: But whoever, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, engages himself in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, he excels.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Perform your bounden duty, for action is superior to inaction, and even the maintenance of the body would not be possible for you through inaction.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment
verses.theme: Perform your prescribed duties — action is better than inaction
verses.meaning: Perform your prescribed duty — action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would be impossible without action. For someone stuck in procrastination or paralysis.

verses.translation: The world is bound by actions other than those performed for the sake of sacrifice; do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), perform actions for that sake alone, free from attachment.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The Creator, having in the beginning created mankind together with sacrifice, said, "By this shall you propagate; let this be the milch cow of your desires—the cow that yields all the desired objects."
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: With this, nourish the gods, and may the gods nourish you; thus, nourishing each other, you shall attain the highest good.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will give you the desired objects. So, he who enjoys the objects given by the gods without offering anything in return is indeed a thief.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The righteous who eat the remnants of the sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those sinful ones who cook food solely for their own sake indeed consume sin.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: From food come forth beings; from rain, food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain, and sacrifice is born of action.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Know that action comes from Brahma, and Brahma comes from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervasive Brahma ever rests in sacrifice.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion, who is of sinful life, rejoicing in the senses, lives in vain, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: But for that man who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self and is content in the Self alone, indeed there is nothing to do.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: For him, there is no interest whatsoever in what is done or not done; nor does he depend on any being for any purpose.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the actions that should be done; for by performing actions without attachment, one reaches the Supreme.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment
verses.theme: Always do your work without attachment — you reach the Supreme
verses.meaning: Therefore without attachment, perform action as a matter of duty — for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme. For burnout from working only for recognition or reward.

verses.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection indeed through action alone; even with the intention of protecting the masses, you should perform action.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Whatever a great man does, others also do; whatever he establishes as the standard, the world follows.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment
verses.theme: Whatever great people do, others follow their example
verses.meaning: Whatever action a great person performs, common people follow. And whatever standards they set by exemplary acts, all the world pursues. For someone who wants to lead or influence others.

verses.translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that needs to be done by Me, nor is there anything unattained that needs to be attained; yet I engage Myself in action.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: For, should I not ever engage myself in action, unwearied, people would in every way follow my path, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: These worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I would be the author of confusion of castes and destruction of these beings.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: As the ignorant act out of attachment to action, O Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing for the welfare of the world.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Let no wise man unsettle the minds of ignorant people who are attached to action; he should engage them in all actions, himself fulfilling them with devotion.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: All actions are wrought in all cases by the qualities of Nature alone. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment
verses.theme: All actions are performed by nature — the ego falsely claims 'I am the doer'
verses.meaning: All actions are performed by the modes of material nature. But one whose mind is deluded by ego thinks 'I am the doer.' For someone crushed by the pressure of believing they must control everything.

verses.translation: But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed Arjuna, about the divisions of the qualities and their functions, knowing that the Gunas, as senses, move amidst the Gunas, as the sense-objects, is not attached.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Those deluded by the qualities of Nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish one who is of imperfect knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind centered on the Self, free from hope and egoism, and from mental fever, fight thou.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Those who constantly practice this teaching of Mine with faith and without caviling, they too are freed from actions.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: But those who criticize My teaching and do not practice it, deprived of all knowledge and lacking discernment, know them to be doomed to destruction.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Even a wise man acts in accordance with his own nature; beings will follow their nature; what can restraint do?
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses; let no one come under their sway; for, they are his enemies.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment
verses.theme: Better your own duty imperfect than another's duty perfect
verses.meaning: It is far better to do your own duty imperfectly than to do another's perfectly. To die in one's own duty is better — performing another's duty is dangerous. For someone living by others' expectations or comparing their path to someone else's.

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "But what compels man to commit sin, even against his wishes, O Varshneya (Krishna), as if constrained by force?"
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "It is desire and it is anger, both of the quality of Rajas, all-devouring and all-sinful; know this as the foe here in this world."
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, and as an embryo is surrounded by the amniotic sac, so is this enveloped by that.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, which is insatiable like fire.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these, it deludes the embodied one, veiling their wisdom.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, control your senses first and then kill this sinful thing, which destroys knowledge and realization.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: They say that the senses are superior to the body; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and He (the Self) is superior even to the intellect.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: Thus, knowing Him who is superior to the intellect and restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to conquer.
verses.chTheme: Karma yoga — selfless action without attachment

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; he then told it to Manu; Manu proclaimed it to Ikshvaku.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: This, handed down in regular succession by the royal sages, was known. This Yoga, however, has been lost here over time, O Parantapa (burner of the foes).
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: That same ancient yoga has been today taught to you by me, for you are my devotee and my friend; it is the supreme secret.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "Later was Thy birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun); how am I to understand that Thou hast taught this Yoga from the beginning?"
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "Many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all, but thou knowest not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes)."
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Though I am unborn and of imperishable nature, and though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own nature, I am born by my own Maya.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: When dharma declines, I manifest to restore it
verses.meaning: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice and a predominant rise of irreligion — at that time I manifest myself. For someone who feels the world is unjust and wonders where God is.

verses.translation: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: I appear to deliver the pious and annihilate the miscreants
verses.meaning: To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of dharma, I appear in every age. For someone who needs faith that good ultimately prevails.

verses.translation: He who thus knows, in their true light, My divine birth and actions, having abandoned the body, is not born again; he comes to Me, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained My Being.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: In whatever way men approach Me, even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: As people surrender to me, I reward them accordingly
verses.meaning: As all surrender unto me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows my path in all respects. For someone who questions whether their chosen spiritual path or approach matters.

verses.translation: Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; for success is quickly attained by men through action.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; though I am the author of it, know Me as non-doer and immutable.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Having known this, the ancient seekers of freedom also performed action; therefore, do thou also perform action, as the ancients did in days of yore.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. Therefore, I shall teach you the nature of action and inaction, by knowing which you will be liberated from the evil of Samsara, the wheel of birth and death.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: For verily, the true nature of action enjoined by the scriptures should be known, as well as that of forbidden or unlawful action, and of inaction; the nature of action is hard to understand.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a yogi and performer of all actions.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: See inaction in action and action in inaction — this is wisdom
verses.meaning: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is intelligent among humans. Such a person is a yogi and has accomplished everything. For someone at a more advanced stage of spiritual practice.

verses.translation: He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and selfish purposes, and whose actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge, the wise call him a sage.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything even while being engaged in activity.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: Abandoning attachment to results, always content — one does nothing even while doing everything
verses.meaning: Abandoning all attachment to the results of activities, ever satisfied and independent — they do nothing even while doing everything. For someone exhausted from grasping at outcomes.

verses.translation: Without hope, controlling the mind and the self, having abandoned all covetousness, and performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Content with what comes to him without effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, he acts yet is not bound.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: To one who is devoid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is dissolved.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman indeed shall be attained by one who always sees Brahman in action.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others, who have realized the Self, offer the Self as sacrifice in the fire of Brahman alone.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as a sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as a sacrifice in the fire of the senses.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy, or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Others again offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as sacrifice, while ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer the study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the restraint of the breath.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in each life-breath. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed through sacrifice.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then can they have the other, O Arjuna?
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman at the face of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action, and thus knowing, you shall be liberated.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacrifice with objects, O Parantapa (scorcher of the foes). All actions in their entirety, O Arjuna, culminate in knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Know that the wise who have realized the truth will instruct thee in that knowledge through long prostration, supplication, and service.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Knowing that thou shalt not, O Arjuna, again be deluded like this; and by that thou shalt see all beings in thyself and also in me.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet thou shalt surely cross over all sins by the raft of knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ash.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it within the Self in due time.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: Nothing in this world is as purifying as wisdom — found within in time
verses.meaning: There is nothing in this world as purifying as wisdom. And in time, the practitioner who is sincere finds this within themselves automatically. For someone on a spiritual search who feels they haven't found it yet.

verses.translation: The one who is full of faith, devoted to it, and has subdued their senses obtains this knowledge; and upon obtaining the knowledge, they attain the supreme peace immediately.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self go to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting one.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: He who has renounced actions through Yoga, whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge, and who is self-possessed—such a one is not bound by actions, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action

verses.translation: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge (of the Self), cut asunder the doubt of the self, born of ignorance, residing in your heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna!
verses.chTheme: Knowledge, wisdom, and the nature of action
verses.theme: Cut the doubt born of ignorance with the sword of knowledge — arise
verses.meaning: Cut away the doubt born of ignorance that is lodged in your heart with the sword of knowledge. Arise — take refuge in yoga. For someone paralysed by doubt who needs to act on what they know.

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga. Please tell me conclusively which is better of the two."
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action."
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He should be known as a perpetual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily freed from bondage.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action, or the performance of action, as though they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one, obtains the fruits of both.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is also reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one, sees truly.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: But, O mighty-armed Arjuna, renunciation is hard to attain without Yoga; the sage who is in harmony with Yoga quickly goes to Brahman.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is pure, who has conquered the self, who has subdued his senses, and who realizes his Self as the Self in all beings, though acting, is not tainted.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonized knower of Truth think, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening, and closing the eyes, one should be convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not tainted by water.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined
verses.theme: Act without attachment like a lotus untouched by water
verses.meaning: One who performs action offering all results to the Supreme and abandoning attachment is not touched by sinful reaction — just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water. For someone who wants to engage fully in life without being consumed by it.

verses.translation: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only through the body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, for the purification of the self.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: The one who is united (the well-poised or harmonized) having abandoned the fruit of action attains eternal peace; whereas the one who is not united (the unsteady or unbalanced), impelled by desire and attached to the fruit, is bound.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Mentally renouncing all actions and being self-controlled, the embodied one happily rests in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing others (body and senses) to act.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Neither does the Lord create agency nor actions for the world, nor union with the fruits of actions; rather, it is Nature that acts.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: The Lord takes neither the demerit nor the merit of any; knowledge is enveloped by ignorance, and beings are deluded.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: But to those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, like the sun, knowledge reveals the Supreme Brahman.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Their intellect absorbed in That, their self being That, established in That, with That as their supreme goal, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Sages look with an equal eye on a Brahmana endowed with learning and humility, on a cow, an elephant, a dog, and even an outcaste.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined
verses.theme: The wise see all living beings with equal vision
verses.meaning: The humble sage by virtue of true knowledge sees with equal vision a learned brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater. For someone caught in comparison, prejudice, or seeing themselves as lesser or greater.

verses.translation: Even here in this world, those whose minds rest in reality overcome birth; Brahman is indeed spotless and real; therefore they are established in Brahman.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Resting in Brahman, with a steady intellect and undeluded, the knower of Brahman neither rejoices upon obtaining what is pleasant nor grieves upon obtaining what is unpleasant.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined
verses.theme: The wise person is not elated by good nor disturbed by bad
verses.meaning: One who is not disturbed in mind even amidst threefold misery, nor elated in happiness, and is free from attachment, fear and anger — is called a sage of steady mind. For someone whose emotions swing wildly with circumstances.

verses.translation: With the self unattached to external contacts, he finds happiness in the Self; with the self engaged in the meditation of Brahman, he attains endless happiness.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: The enjoyments that arise from contact are only sources of pain, for they have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna; the wise do not rejoice in them.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He who is able, while still here in this world, to withstand the impulse born out of desire and anger before the liberation from the body, he is a Yogi, and he is a happy man.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He who is happy within, who rejoices within, and who is illuminated within, that Yogi attains absolute freedom, or Moksha, becoming Brahman himself.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: The sages obtain absolute freedom or Moksha when their sins have been destroyed, their dualities have been torn asunder, they are self-controlled, and they are intent on the welfare of all beings.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: Absolute freedom exists on all sides for those self-controlled ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled their thoughts, and who have realized the Self.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined
verses.theme: Those free from desire and anger, who have controlled the mind, find liberation everywhere
verses.meaning: Those who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled the mind and have realized the self — liberation is present for them everywhere. For someone who wants practical freedom from anger.

verses.translation: Shutting out all external contacts and fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, realizing the outgoing and incoming breaths moving within the nostrils.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: With the senses, mind, and intellect ever controlled, having liberation as their supreme goal, free from desire, fear, and anger, the sage is truly liberated forever.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined

verses.translation: He who knows Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, attains peace.
verses.chTheme: Renunciation and the yoga of action combined
verses.theme: Knowing Krishna as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and the friend of all — one attains peace
verses.meaning: The sages attain peace by knowing me as the ultimate purpose of all sacrifices, the ruler of all worlds, and the true friend of all living entities. For someone searching for peace and a sense of being supported.

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions—he is a sannyasi and a yogi, not he who is without fire and without action.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Do you, O Arjuna, know that Yoga is what they call renunciation; no one indeed becomes a Yogi who has not renounced their thoughts.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained Yoga, inaction is said to be the means.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: When a person is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then they are said to have attained Yoga.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: One should raise oneself by one's own self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the self alone is one's own friend, and the self alone is one's own enemy.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: Elevate yourself — your mind is your best friend and worst enemy
verses.meaning: Let a man lift himself by his own self. Let him not degrade himself — for the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. For anyone who is their own biggest obstacle.

verses.translation: The Self is the friend of the self of him by whom the Self has been conquered; but to the unconquered self, this Self stands in the position of an enemy, like an external foe.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: For one who has conquered the mind it is the best friend — for one who has not, it is the worst enemy
verses.meaning: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. But for one who has failed to do so, the mind will remain the greatest enemy. For chronic self-doubt or inner conflict.

verses.translation: The Supreme Self of him who is self-controlled and peaceful remains balanced in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: The Yogi who is satisfied with the knowledge and wisdom of the Self, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and gold are all the same, is said to have attained Nirvikalpa Samadhi.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: He who is of the same mind towards the good-hearted, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relatives, the righteous, and the unrighteous, excels.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Let the yogi constantly strive to keep the mind steady, remaining in solitude, alone, with the body and mind controlled, and free from hope and greed.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of cloth, skin, and kusha grass layered one over the other.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practice Yoga for the purification of the self.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Let him firmly hold his body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose without looking around.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled their mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let them sit, having Me as their supreme goal.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Thus, always keeping the mind balanced, the yogi, with the mind controlled, attains the peace abiding in Me, culminating in liberation.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Verily, Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is always awake, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: Yoga is not for one who eats or sleeps too much or too little
verses.meaning: There is no possibility of becoming a yogi for one who eats too much or too little, sleeps too much or too little. Yoga becomes possible for the regulated person. For destructive daily habits or extremes.

verses.translation: Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such as walking, etc.), who exercises moderation in action, and who is moderate in sleep and wakefulness.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: Regulated eating, movement, sleep and wakefulness eliminates all pain
verses.meaning: One who is regulated in eating, sleeping, recreation and work can mitigate all material pains by practicing yoga. For someone whose pain is made worse by unregulated living.

verses.translation: When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any of the objects of desire, then it is said, 'He is united'.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker, so is the Yogi of a controlled mind, who practices Yoga in the Self, compared.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: A lamp in a windless place does not flicker — the disciplined mind in meditation
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — this is the simile used for the yogi whose mind is controlled and who is absorbed in meditation. For building a meditation or focus practice.

verses.translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, attains quietude, and when one sees the Self by the Self, they are satisfied in their own Self.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: When he (the Yogi) feels that infinite bliss which can be grasped by the pure intellect and which transcends the senses, and is established therein, never moving away from the reality.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Having obtained it, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; established in it, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Let this be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undespairing mind.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Abandoning unreservedly all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of senses by the mind from all sides.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Little by little, let him attain steadiness of the intellect by holding it firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything else.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it from that and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: Wherever the mind wanders — bring it back under control of the self
verses.meaning: Wherever the mind wanders due to its flickering and unsteady nature — bring it back under the control of the self. For anyone practising mindfulness or struggling with a scattered mind.

verses.translation: Supreme Bliss indeed comes to this Yogi whose mind is made peaceful, whose passion is quelled, who has become Brahman, and who is free from sin.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: The yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of yoga), is freed from sins and easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: With the mind harmonized by Yoga, he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, never becomes separated from Me, nor do I from him.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me never loses me and I never lose them
verses.meaning: For one who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me — I am never lost to them, nor are they ever lost to me. For someone who feels spiritually disconnected or abandoned by God.

verses.translation: He who, being established in unity, worships Me, who dwells in all beings, that yogi abides in Me, whatever their mode of living may be.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees reality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, is regarded as the highest Yogi.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, I do not see how this Yoga of equanimity, which you have taught me, can be maintained steadily, due to the restlessness of the mind."
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: The mind is indeed restless, turbulent, strong, and unyielding, O Krishna; I consider it as difficult to control as controlling the wind.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: The mind is restless, turbulent, obstinate and very strong — controlling it seems as difficult as controlling the wind
verses.meaning: The mind is restless, turbulent, obstinate and very strong — controlling it seems as difficult as controlling the wind. Arjuna voices what we all feel. For someone who feels their mind is impossible to tame.

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but with practice and dispassion, it can be restrained."
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
verses.theme: The restless mind can be controlled by practice and detachment
verses.meaning: It is undoubtedly very difficult to curb the restless mind — but it is possible through practice and detachment. For someone who feels they cannot control their thoughts or anxiety.

verses.translation: I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one with an uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain it by the appropriate means.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "He who is unable to control himself, even though he has faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he meet, having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, O Krishna?"
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a rent cloud, supportless, O mighty-armed one, deluded on the path of Brahman?
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: O Krishna, please completely dispel this doubt of mine, for it is not possible for anyone but You to do so.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the next will there be destruction for him; none, indeed, who does good, O my son, ever comes to grief."
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control

verses.translation: Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is born in a house of the pure and wealthy.
verses.chTheme: Dhyana yoga — meditation and mind control
