verses.translation: Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds come forth as enemies of the world, intent on its destruction.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance, holding evil ideas due to delusion, they work with impure intentions.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Giving themselves over to immeasurable cares that end only with death, regarding the gratification of lust as their highest aim, and feeling sure that that is all.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain hoards of wealth by unlawful means for sensual enjoyment.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: "I have gained this today; I will fulfill this desire of mine; this is mine, and this wealth will be mine in the future."
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: "I have slain that enemy, and I shall slay others too. I am the Lord; I enjoy, I am perfect, powerful, and happy."
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: "I am wealthy and born into a noble family. Who is my equal? I shall perform sacrifices, give charity, and rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Bewildered by many fancies, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego
verses.theme: Bewildered by many anxieties, entangled in delusion — too attached to sense gratification
verses.meaning: Bewildered by many anxieties and entangled in a network of illusions, they are too attached to sense gratification and fall into a foul hell. For someone obsessively chasing status, validation or pleasure.

verses.translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust, and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Those cruel haters, the worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, they do not attain Me, thus falling, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: There are three gates to this hell, destructive of the self: lust, anger, and greed; therefore, one should abandon these three.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego
verses.theme: Lust, anger and greed — the three gates to self-destruction
verses.meaning: There are three gates leading to self-destructive hell — lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul. For repeating destructive patterns.

verses.translation: A person who is liberated from these three gates of darkness, O Arjuna, practices what is beneficial for them and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, does not attain perfection, nor happiness, nor the Supreme Goal.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act in this world.
verses.chTheme: Divine and demoniac natures — virtue vs ego

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "What is the condition of those who, disregarding the injunctions of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith—is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas, O Krishna?"
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "There are threefold faiths inherent in the nature of the embodied: the sattvic (pure), the rajasic (passionate), and the tamasic (dark). Hear of them."
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The faith of each is in accordance with their nature, O Arjuna. People consist of their faith; as a person's faith is, so are they.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship
verses.theme: The faith of each person is in accordance with their nature
verses.meaning: The faith of each person is in accordance with their nature. The human being is made of faith — whatever faith one has, that is what one becomes. For someone questioning their beliefs or spiritual type.

verses.translation: The sattvic, or pure, men worship the gods; the rajasic, or passionate, worship the yakshas and rakshasas; the others, the tamasic or deluded people, worship ghosts and hosts of nature-spirits.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Those men who practice terrific austerities not prescribed by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, driven by the force of lust and attachment.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Know thou these to be of demonical resolves, senselessly torturing all the elements in the body and Me who dwell in the body.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The food that is dear to each is threefold, as well as sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Hear the distinction of these.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savory, oily, substantial, and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief, and disease.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: That which is stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, rejected, and impure is the food liked by the Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward, as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that doing so is their duty, is Sattvic or pure.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The sacrifice that is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for show, know that to be a Rajasic Yajna.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, and which is devoid of mantras, gifts, and faith.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers, and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-injury are all called the austerities of the body.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Speech that causes no excitement, is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial; the practice of studying the Vedas is called austerity of speech.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, and purity of nature—this is called mental austerity.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: This threefold austerity, practiced by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, is called Sattvic.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship
verses.theme: Austerity of mind — serenity, silence, self-control, purity — is the highest
verses.meaning: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of thought — this is called austerity of the mind. For someone building mental and spiritual discipline.

verses.translation: The austerity that is practiced with the aim of gaining good reception, honor, and worship, and with hypocrisy, is said to be Rajasic, unstable, and transient.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be of the Tamasic nature.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a suitable place and time to a worthy person, is held to be Sattvic.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: And, that gift which is given with the intention of receiving something in return, or expecting a reward, or begrudgingly, is considered to be Rajasic.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The gift that is given in the wrong place and at the wrong time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult, is declared to be of a Tamasic nature.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that, the Brahmanas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices were created formerly.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Therefore, with the utterance of "Om," the acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity, as enjoined in the scriptures, are always begun by the students of Brahman.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Uttering "Tat," without aiming for the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice, austerity, and the various acts of gifts performed by those seeking liberation.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: The word "Sat" is used to refer to reality and goodness; likewise, O Arjuna, the word "Sat" is used to refer to an auspicious act.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is also called 'Sat', and action in connection with these, or for the sake of the Supreme, is also called 'Sat'.
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Whatever is sacrificed, given, or performed, and whatever austerity is practiced without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is of no value here or hereafter (after death).
verses.chTheme: Three types of faith — goodness passion ignorance in worship

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O mighty-armed Hrishikesa, I desire to know the essence or truth of renunciation and abandonment severally, O slayer of Kesi."
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "The sages understand sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions to be tyaga."
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as evil; while others declare that acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be relinquished.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, indeed, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; for sacrifice, gift, and austerity are the purifiers of the wise.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: But even these actions should be performed, leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is my certain and most assured conviction.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Verily, the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same out of delusion is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: He who abandons action out of fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by performing such Rajasic renunciation.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as sattvic (pure).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate an unpleasant task nor is he attached to a pleasant one.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Indeed, it is not possible for an embodied being to completely abandon actions; however, he who relinquishes the rewards of actions is truly called a man of renunciation.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: It is impossible to give up all activity — but giving up the fruits makes one a true renouncer
verses.meaning: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up all activities. But one who renounces the fruits of action is said to be a true renouncer. For someone who wants to escape everything to find peace.

verses.translation: The threefold fruit of action (evil, good, and mixed) accrues after death to those who do not abandon it, but never to those who do.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes, as declared in the Sankhya system, for the accomplishment of all actions.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The body, the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various kinds, and the presiding deity—the fifth.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Whatever action a person performs with their body, speech, and mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Now, such being the case, verily he who, owing to an untrained understanding, looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence does not see.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted by good or evil, though he slays these people, he does not slay, nor is he bound by the action.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower form the threefold impulse for action; the organ, the action, and the agent form the threefold basis of action.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Knowledge, action, and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these, hear duly.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That by which one sees the indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in any of them—know that knowledge to be Sattvic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: Seeing one imperishable reality in all divided things — that is pure knowledge
verses.meaning: That knowledge by which one sees one undivided imperishable reality in all divided living beings — know that knowledge to be pure goodness. For someone seeking to understand unity or non-duality.

verses.translation: But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as being distinct from one another, know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without any foundation in Truth, and is trivial—that is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: An action that is ordained, free from attachment, done without love or hatred, and without desire for reward is declared to be Sattvic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfillment of desires or gain with egotism or with much effort is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard for the consequences, loss, injury, and one's own ability, is declared to be Tamasic (dark).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is considered to be of a Sattvic (pure) nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of their actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Unsteady, vulgar, inflexible, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—such an agent is called Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness, according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what should be done and what should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation—that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That by which one wrongly understands dharma and adharma, and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done—that intellect, O Arjuna, is rajasic (passionate).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That intellect, O Arjuna, which is enveloped in darkness and sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted, is Tamasic (dark).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The unwavering firmness, through which Yoga restrains the functions of the mind, life-force, and senses—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: But that, O Arjuna, by which one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures, and earning of wealth, on account of attachment and desire for reward—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That firmness, O Arjuna, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and conceit, is Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: And now, O Arjuna, hear from Me of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices through practice and surely comes to the end of pain.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar—that happiness is declared to be sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to self-realization.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That happiness which arises from the contact of the senses with the objects, which is initially like nectar but eventually like poison, is said to be Rajasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: That happiness which at first, as well as in the end, deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: There is no being on earth or in heaven among the gods that is liberated from the three qualities born of Nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the qualities born of their own nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, and uprightness, as well as knowledge, realization, and belief in God, are the duties of Brahmanas, born of their own nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Prowess, splendor, firmness, dexterity, and not fleeing from battle, generosity, and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of their own nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of their own nature; and service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of their own nature.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Each person devoted to their own duty attains perfection. How they attain perfection while being engaged in their own duty, hear now.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: By doing one's own duty wholeheartedly, a person attains perfection
verses.meaning: By following their own occupation, every person can achieve perfection. By worshipping the source of all beings through their occupation, a person can attain success. For someone who questions whether their work or role has meaning.

verses.translation: He from whom all the beings have evolved and by whom all this is pervaded, worshipping Him with his own duty, one attains perfection.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Better is one's own duty, even if it is destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: Better your own dharma imperfect than another's dharma perfect
verses.meaning: It is better to engage in one's own occupation even if done imperfectly than to accept the occupation of another and perform it perfectly. For someone living someone else's life.

verses.translation: One should not, O Arjuna, abandon the duty to which one is born, though it may be faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, just as fire is by smoke.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled, he attains the supreme state of freedom from action through renunciation.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Learn from Me, O Arjuna, in brief how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman—the Eternal, that supreme state of knowledge.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self through firmness, relinquishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Dwelling in solitude, eating sparingly, with speech, body, and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, and resorting to dispassion.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger, and covetousness, and being free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires; he is the same to all beings, and obtains supreme devotion to Me.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: By devotion, he knows Me in truth, who and what I am; then, having known Me in truth, he immediately enters into the Supreme.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: By devotion one knows me — then enters me
verses.meaning: One can understand me as I am — the Supreme — only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of me by such devotion, they can enter my kingdom. For someone who wants a direct, personal relationship with the divine.

verses.translation: Having taken refuge in Me and doing all actions, by My grace he obtains the eternal, indestructible state of being.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, and resorting to the yoga of discrimination, do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Fixing your mind on Me, you shall, by My grace, overcome all obstacles; but if you will not hear Me due to egoism, you shall perish.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight," then thy resolve is vain; nature will compel thee.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: O Arjuna, bound by your own Karma (action) born of your own nature, that which from delusion you wish not to do, even that you shall do helplessly.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusory power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Fly to Him for refuge with all your being, O Arjuna; by His grace you will obtain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Thus, wisdom more secret than secrecy itself has been declared to you by me. Reflect on it fully, then act as you wish.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: Reflect on this fully — then do as you choose
verses.meaning: I have now explained to you the most confidential of all knowledge. Reflect on this fully — then do as you choose. For someone who needs permission to trust their own judgment after receiving guidance.

verses.translation: Hear again My supreme word, most secret of all; for you are dearly beloved of Me, I will tell you what is good.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. You will come to Me; I truly promise you this, for you are dear to Me.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: Fix your mind on me, be devoted, worship me — you will come to me
verses.meaning: Always think of me, become my devotee, worship me and offer your homage to me. By doing so you will certainly come to me. This I promise you because you are my very dear friend. For someone who wants a personal commitment to God.

verses.translation: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone; I will liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
verses.theme: Abandon all duties and surrender to me — I will free you from all reactions
verses.meaning: Abandon all varieties of duties and simply surrender to me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions — do not fear. For someone completely overwhelmed who needs to let go entirely and trust.

verses.translation: Never speak this to one who is devoid of austerities or devotion, who does not render service, who does not desire to listen, or who cavils at Me.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: He who, with supreme devotion to Me, teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, shall undoubtedly come to Me.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: There is no one among men who does service dearer to Me, nor shall there be anyone on earth dearer to Me than him.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: And he who studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped through the sacrifice of wisdom; such is my conviction.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Also, the man who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds, and be liberated.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with one-pointed focus? Has the delusion of your ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "My delusion has been destroyed, for I have gained my knowledge (memory) through Your grace, O Krishna. I am now free from doubts. I will act according to Your word."
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Sanjaya said, Thus, I have heard this wonderful dialogue between Krishna and the high-souled Arjuna, which causes one's hair to stand on end.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga, directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I continually rejoice.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: And, remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, I am filled with great wonder, O King; and I rejoice again and again.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion

verses.translation: Wherever Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, is; and wherever Arjuna, the wielder of the bow, is; there is prosperity, victory, happiness, and a firm policy; this is my conviction.
verses.chTheme: Moksha through renunciation — ultimate conclusion
